attachments.insertion_landmark: coronoid process of mandible (via a fan-shaped tendon)

actions: posterior fibers retract a protruded mandible

functional_compartments.name: Anterior part (near-vertical fibers)
functional_compartments.function_note: Near-vertical fiber orientation gives the anterior part the largest elevating moment arm; the primary contributor to bite force.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

functional_compartments.name: Posterior part (near-horizontal fibers)
functional_compartments.function_note: Near-horizontal fiber orientation over the posterior temporal fossa gives this part a retractive (posteriorly-directed) moment arm, mainly recruited to retract a protruded mandible rather than to elevate it -- a real fiber-direction-driven functional split within one named muscle.
functional_compartments.source: van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Terminologia Anatomica (FICAT 1998); van Eijden TM, Korfage JA, Brugman P (1997) Anat Rec 248(3):464-474 -- architecture of the human jaw-closing and jaw-opening muscles (masseter, temporalis, medial/lateral pterygoid): fascicle length, pennation angle and PCSA by head/region

ultrasound_injection_approach.transducer_placement: Over the temporal fossa, superior to the zygomatic arch, spanning the anterior and middle thirds of the fan (the fibers most active in clenching); the posterior third mainly retracts the mandible and is a less common target.
ultrasound_injection_approach.depth_layer: Directly on the temporal bone within the temporal fossa, deep to the temporalis fascia (itself deep to subcutaneous fat and the temporoparietal fascia).
ultrasound_injection_approach.identification_cues: Bulges on clenching, most palpably over the anterior fibers just above the zygomatic arch.
structures_at_risk: superficial temporal artery and vein, and the auriculotemporal nerve, all running superficial to the temporalis fascia rather than through the muscle itself
ultrasound_injection_approach.notes: Injected for bruxism and masticatory myofascial pain alongside masseter, typically at 2-3 points across the anterior and middle fibers.
ultrasound_injection_approach.source: Gray's Anatomy for Students, 4th ed. (Drake, Vogl, Mitchell); Moore KL, Dalley AF, Agur AMR, Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 8th ed.

trigger_points.location_description: TrP1, anterior fibres above the zygomatic arch.
trigger_points.activation_perpetuating_factors: Bruxism, clenching, prolonged opening, occlusal disharmony, forward-head posture, chilling; satellite to sternocleidomastoid and upper trapezius trigger points.
trigger_points.notes: Tooth hypersensitivity to temperature can accompany referral from any of the four temporalis trigger-point zones.
trigger_points.source: Simons, Travell & Simons Trigger Point Manual -- as cited in this atlas's uploaded head and neck muscle reference document (Simons DG, Travell JG, Simons LS, Myofascial Pain and Dysfunction: The Trigger Point Manual, Vol 1, 2nd ed., Williams & Wilkins, 1999; Donnelly JM, Fernandez-de-las-Penas C, Finnegan M, Freeman JL (eds), 3rd ed., Wolters Kluwer, 2019)
